neet_phy_u13_t06_1.working: In a radial field the plane of the coil stays parallel to B at every position. So the torque is NIAB, which is balanced by kθ. This gives θ = (NAB/k)·I, so deflection is proportional to current.

neet_phy_u13_t06_2.working: S = Ig·G/(I − Ig) = 0.01×99/0.99 = 1 Ω. The shunt is connected in parallel.

neet_phy_u13_t06_3.working: R = V/Ig − G = 10/0.005 − 40 = 2000 − 40 = 1960 Ω. The resistance is connected in series.

neet_phy_u13_t06_4.working: The soft iron core concentrates the field and raises B. Current sensitivity is NAB/k, so it increases with B. Both statements are true and R explains A.

neet_phy_u13_t06_5.working: I: Doubling N with the same wire doubles the wire length, so R doubles. Voltage sensitivity NAB/(kR) is therefore unchanged, so I is false. II: A parallel combination has resistance less than either resistor, so II is true.
